goal: Complete the CODEREF-CORE unified-pipeline migration boundary without removing the live lightweight scanner: make PipelineOrchestrator generators the only writers of canonical .coderef artifact paths; quarantine or deprecate competing src/fileGeneration public writers while retaining shared index-storage and route serializers; resolve the ContextGenerator and package-entrypoint export split; remove the redundant coderef-scan leg from default pipeline and full-watch execution; classify and migrate remaining legacy scanner callers; and add compatibility, overwrite-contract, orchestration, build, and package-entrypoint tests. Out of scope: removing scanCurrentElements, removing shared index or route helpers, changing artifact semantics beyond contract normalization, or redoing the completed TreeSitterScanner retirement.

phases.name: Audit and lock the migration boundary
phases.description: Reconfirm production callers and artifact contracts, capture the baseline, and encode the intended boundary as tests before changing public surfaces.

tasks.description: Reconfirm the live migration boundary from code: inventory every production caller and public export of scanCurrentElements, src/fileGeneration writers, both ContextGenerator classes, coderef-pipeline, and coderef-watch; classify each surface as canonical writer, retained lightweight API, shared serializer, compatibility shim, or retirement candidate.

Capture the current schemas and ownership of every canonical output path written by both generations, especially graph.json, context, coverage, drift, patterns, validation, index variants, routes, and frontend-calls; record which legacy writers can overwrite a richer pipeline artifact under the same filename.
Run the existing build, unit/integration suites, CLI tests, and package-entrypoint smoke checks to establish a BEFORE baseline for compatibility and generated-artifact behavior.

Add focused failing contract tests that demonstrate the intended boundary: canonical artifact paths have one schema owner, legacy APIs cannot silently clobber them, the public ContextGenerator identity is consistent, and the default pipeline does not perform a redundant scanner pass.

phases.name: Protect canonical artifacts and neutralize shared serializers
phases.description: Quarantine competing legacy writers, preserve compatibility deliberately, and move genuinely shared serialization infrastructure behind a neutral boundary.

tasks.description: Quarantine or deprecate competing src/fileGeneration artifact writers behind an explicit legacy compatibility surface, removing ambiguous root exports while preserving a documented compatibility path where semver requires it. Do not remove scanCurrentElements.

Extract or re-home the actively shared index-storage and route/frontend-call serialization helpers under a neutral artifact/serialization module; update unified generators to import the neutral module and leave thin compatibility re-exports only where necessary.
Verify canonical populate output against the locked schemas and prove that invoking any retained legacy compatibility API cannot replace canonical graph/report artifacts with incompatible shapes.
Commit the canonical artifact-writer boundary and shared-serializer relocation using explicit pathspecs on main after the focused contract tests pass.

phases.name: Unify public API names and package entrypoints
phases.description: Resolve the ContextGenerator collision and make every supported runtime and declaration entrypoint expose the same intentional API.

tasks.description: Resolve the ContextGenerator name collision by giving the legacy scanner-backed context service and PipelineState artifact generator unambiguous names, with one intentional canonical export and explicit compatibility aliases as needed.

Reconcile package.json main/types/exports and the root and src barrels so bare-package resolution, CommonJS/ESM consumers, TypeScript declarations, and direct supported entrypoints expose the same canonical API contract.
Build the package and test runtime plus declaration resolution through every supported entrypoint, including the canonical ContextGenerator export and any intentional legacy subpath.
Commit the public API and package-entrypoint alignment with explicit pathspecs after compatibility tests pass.

phases.name: Remove redundant orchestration and validate the final boundary
phases.description: Eliminate the default double scan, settle remaining legacy scanner callers, and prove the complete build, package, CLI, watch, and artifact contracts before close.

tasks.description: Remove or redefine the default coderef-pipeline scan leg so a full pipeline/watch run parses the project once through populate-coderef; retain coderef-scan as an explicit lightweight diagnostic command rather than an implicit pre-populate pass.

Classify the remaining scanner callers: preserve scanCurrentElements as a lightweight API, migrate the legacy context caller to the canonical boundary, and either integrate, explicitly expose, or retire the unused scanner FileWatcher without changing the modern coderef-watch contract.

Add orchestration tests proving default pipeline and full watch perform one canonical scan, standalone coderef-scan remains functional, incremental watch remains functional, and no retired FileWatcher or legacy writer path is reached in production flows.

Run the full unit/integration suite, build, package dry-run, CLI smoke tests, canonical populate/validate cycle, and generated-artifact schema checks; compare results to the Phase 1 baseline and investigate every unexplained delta.
Commit orchestration and legacy-caller cleanup using explicit pathspecs on main, then report the final retained/deprecated/removed surface inventory for close-workorder review.

hard_stops.reason: Final operator review is required after compatibility, orchestration, package, and canonical artifact validation complete.

acceptance_criteria: PipelineOrchestrator generators are the only production writers of canonical .coderef graph and report paths, and retained legacy APIs cannot overwrite those files with incompatible schemas.
scanCurrentElements remains available as an explicitly lightweight scanning API, while every remaining scanner caller is classified as retained, migrated, exposed, or retired.
The public ContextGenerator identity and TypeScript declarations are consistent through every supported package entrypoint, with any legacy compatibility alias explicit and tested.
Default coderef-pipeline and full coderef-watch execution perform one canonical scan, while standalone coderef-scan and incremental watch continue to work.
Shared index-storage and route/frontend-call serializers remain functional behind a neutral non-legacy module boundary.
The full test suite, build, package dry-run, CLI smoke tests, populate/validate cycle, and generated-artifact contract tests pass without unexplained regressions.
